Garnacho is a player Aston Villa manager Unai Emery has wanted for over a year now. The 22-year-old is the type of winger -- fast, runs in behind and keeps the touchline wide to stretch the pitch -- that Villa do not have, so his addition makes sense.

Chelsea would have much preferred this to be a permanent deal but, due to a very complex situation involving UEFA financial settlement agreements and rules on swap deals, Villa could not agree to one. This transfer could become permanent if Garnacho makes a certain number of appearances -- but as the Harvey Elliott debacle last season showed, nothing is guaranteed.

July 22

Casemiro

Free
Manchester United: B-

Inter Miami: B

Casemiro's time at Man United was a true rollercoaster. When he announced his exit in January it may have felt like a relief for the fans, but then by the end of the season, they were left wondering how they would replace the nine (!) league goals he chipped in with in 2025-26.

Now 34, he is visibly slow across the pitch and struggles to play in big spaces. Presumably that is less of an issue in MLS, which is several steps down from the Premier League, but it is something to watch with keen interest.

July 21

Morgan Rogers

£117M ($158M)
Aston Villa: A+

Chelsea: C+

Three weeks after Manchester City broke the record for a British player in Elliot Anderson, Chelsea broke it again -- by £1 million -- to sign Rogers. The 23-year-old enjoyed a brilliant season, contributing 25 goals and assists to Aston Villa's cause as they finished inside the top four and won the Europa League, and featured for England at the 2026 World Cup.

Still, this is a gargantuan move that carries immense risk, regardless of how good the player is, as far more often than not, forwards tend to fall short of the expectation this sort of fee creates.

For Villa, it's a literal jackpot. They're under pressure to generate revenue under the terms of their UEFA settlement agreement, and £117 million is an absolute game-changer. A fee of this size opens up a world of transfer possibilities for them.

July 20

João Gomes

£34M ($46M)
Wolves: C

Aston Villa: A

For roughly the same fee as Youri Tielemans left for (£35 million), Villa have signed Gomes as his replacement. The Brazil midfielder should prove a snug fit in Unai Emery's system, as he progresses the ball well and has the athleticism to track and tackle runners.

The fee, which could rise to £38 million with add-ons, looks cheap for a talented 25-year-old with 10 caps for Brazil and three seasons of Premier League football under his belt. Wolves fans are understandably unhappy with the return.

July 17

Johan Manzambi

£50M ($67M)
Freiburg: A+

Aston Villa: B+

Newcastle agreed a fee for Switzerland's World Cup star Manzambi, but Aston Villa stole in to match the terms and convince the player to join them instead. The 20-year-old had an excellent season with Freiburg -- which culminated in losing the Europa League final to Villa, coincidentally -- and looks a fine young attacking talent.

Just over £50 million is simultaneously good value for Villa, who have shopped outside the Premier League to avoid absurd markups on prices, and an amazing deal for Freiburg, who have more than doubled their record departure, which was previously €25 million for Kevin Schade.

July 16

Mason Greenwood

€39M ($45M)
Marseille: C

Fenerbahce: B

Greenwood's production at Marseille -- 37 goals and 12 assists across two Ligue 1 campaigns -- was phenomenal. For a while, he achieved star status at a club that is notoriously dysfunctional and difficult to remain consistent at.

But heavy praise turned to heavy criticism earlier this year, and for the second time in two years, he has departed a club under a cloud of off-field issues. Marseille have lost a very good striker in negative circumstances, made all the worse by the fact Manchester United took €12.5 million of the fee due to a clause in his 2024 exit from the club.

July 14

Luka Vuskovic

£46M ($61M)
Tottenham Hotspur: B

Brighton: B

Vuskovic is an extremely promising young center back, who was named Bundesliga Rookie of the Month four times last season while on loan at Hamburg, before forcing his way into Croatia's 2026 World Cup squad. He's a titan in the air and a confident ball carrier out from the back.

There is a distinct chance that Spurs have let a superb player go too soon here, and when a savvy club like Brighton want your top prospect, it's usually a signal. But they're in win-now mode and have effectively chosen to roll with experience over potential, so it's Vuskovic out and Jan Paul van Hecke in.

Youri Tielemans

£35M ($47M)
Aston Villa: C+

Manchester United: A-

After Éderson's £35 million transfer from Atalanta collapsed, United moved fast to secure Tielemans for the same fee via a release clause. For a player of this established quality and consistency it is a relative bargain -- although at 29, it's no long-term solution.

The Belgium international midfielder was generally superb for Aston Villa over his three years there and the team visibly missed him when injuries forced him to miss games. If there's a silver lining here, it's that he was reportedly a high earner and the club are under pressure to cut costs under a UEFA settlement agreement.

July 13

Andrey Santos

£48M ($64M)
Chelsea: C+

Manchester United: B+

Understandably put off by the fees paid to sign Mateus Fernandes (£85 million), Sandro Tonali (£92.5 million) and Elliot Anderson (£116 million), Man United have found a significantly cheaper way to bolster their midfield with proven Premier League quality.

Andrey Santos, 22, stepped into the Chelsea XI regularly last season and, over the course of nearly 2,500 minutes, showcased good passing and excellent tackling. He's hardly the kind of player the Blues should be looking to lose, but perhaps there's just not enough football to go around next season as the team isn't in Europe.

July 11

Morten Hjulmand

€40M ($46M)
Sporting CP: B

Atlético Madrid: A-

Long linked to Manchester United while Rúben Amorim was in charge, Hjulmand has finally made the move to one of Europe's top leagues with Atlético. Diego Simeone will love his combativeness, fire, leadership qualities and strength in the air.

A fee of €40 million, plus some modest bonuses, looks a little on the lean side as fees go for Sporting, but the reality is this was probably the maximum you'd get for the 27-year-old once interest from the big-spending Premier League clubs' dropped.

Jeremy Monga

£10M ($13M)
Leicester City: B

Manchester City: B

City outbid Arsenal to secure Monga, who has made the breakthrough to men's football incredibly early. He became the second-youngest Premier League player ever in 2025, aged 15 years and 271 days, and played just shy of 1,000 Championship minutes last season aged 16.

Anyone who makes this kind of leap is worth a look for an elite club, as they could become a homegrown superstar. Whether or not the first-team pathway ever opens up for Monga to impress at City is another question, though.

July 6

Sandro Tonali

£92.5M ($125M)
Newcastle United: A+

Tottenham Hotspur: C-

Tottenham have signed Tonali in a deal that could rise to £100 million with achievable add-ons. It's an astonishing deal and, quite frankly, an astonishing use of £100 million, making him one of the 15 most expensive footballers of all time.

Clearly, Spurs manager Roberto De Zerbi is convinced he can work miracles with his Italian compatriot, but Newcastle likely can't believe their luck. They got just one consistently strong season out of three from Tonali, before offloading him for twice what they spent to acquire him.

July 5

Denzel Dumfries

€20M ($22.8M)
Inter Milan: C

Real Madrid: A

Dumfries is one of the most prolific goalscoring defenders in world football -- although labeling him a defender may be a stretch. A direct, attacking wing back, who spends more time in the opposition box than his own, he can be a real difference-maker from the flank. Losing him for just €20 million via a release clause in his contract is tough for Inter, although the Dutchman's injury issues last season did force the Nerazzurri to learn how to cope without him.

July 3

Nathaniel Brown

€55M ($64M)
Eintracht Frankfurt: A

Bayern Munich: B

Brown's career is moving fast. He used a sensational 2025-26 season with Frankfurt to not only gatecrash Germany's 2026 World Cup squad, but oust David Raum as first-choice left back.

The 23-year-old defender is athletic, very fast, defends one-on-ones well and combines traditional overlapping runs with modern, inverted runs into the box. Born in Bavaria, his signing for Bayern is both a headline move and a homecoming.

Frankfurt won't be able to replace his quality like-for-like, but they have at least secured a fee that makes Brown one of the three most expensive left backs of all time.

July 2

Mateus Fernandes

£85M ($112M)
West Ham United: A+

Tottenham Hotspur: C+

Despite consecutive relegations from the Premier League with Southampton and then West Ham, it is clear Fernandes is an excellent player. An all-round midfielder who can pretty much do it all by the age of 21, there is no doubt Tottenham are looking in the right area here as they seek to improve their midfield.

The price, however, is eye-popping. Even Manchester United, who spent last summer shelling out roughly £65 million per attacker, had to dip out of this race for Fernandes because the quoted transfer price was so high. The Portugal midfielder will have to do incredibly well, for a long time, to prove worth this outlay.

July 1

Anthony Gordon

€70M (£60M, $80M)
Newcastle: A-

Barcelona: B

With legendary goal scorer Robert Lewandowski gone on a free transfer and Manchester United loanee Marcus Rashford far from certain to stay permanently, Barcelona needed a big addition to their forward line this summer. Gordon plays both left wing and striker, presses hard and was the fastest player in the Premier League last season, topping 36 km/h, per Gradient Sports. He's a good fit for Hansi Flick's tactical style.

This is about the right price range for any player of this established quality. Newcastle could earn an extra €10 million if add-ons are met, making this potentially even more lucrative for them.

Marco Palestra

€60M (£48M, $68M)
Atalanta: A

Chelsea: B

If Chelsea intend to play with fully fledged wing backs under new manager Xabi Alonso, signing Palestra makes a lot of sense. The 21-year-old is tall, fast and loves to knock the ball past an opponent -- but he also has neat footwork in tight spaces. The Blues are once again trusting their talent ID, staking a big transfer fee on a player with just one full season under his belt, which came on loan at Cagliari.

Naturally, Atalanta are the big winners here: They watched a player blossom out on loan, become the subject of a bidding war between Inter Milan and Chelsea, and then accepted the highest bid.

Marc Cucurella

€55M (£47M, $64M)
Chelsea: C-

Real Madrid: A-

When Chelsea's ownership group drew up their transfer strategy, this is surely not what it was supposed to look like. Cucurella is one of the few signings that has unequivocally succeeded, yet here they are losing him for a fairly modest fee, potentially rising to €60M with add-ons.

The Blues' loss is Madrid's gain: Barcelona academy graduate Cucurella returns to Spain as a fully fledged international and trophy winner, shoring up the left-back area in Madrid nicely. José Mourinho will love his blood-and-thunder style.

Ismael Saibari

€55M ($64M)
PSV Eindhoven: A

Bayern Munich: B

Saibari has blossomed over the last two years, contributing 52 goals and assists for PSV in the Champions League and Eredivisie play and securing his place as Morocco's first-choice striker. He scored at the 2026 World Cup to further enhance his reputation.

Bayern will appreciate those scoring numbers, but they will also love his ability to drop deep, receive the ball and create. It's what Harry Kane already does for them to a world class level, and now Bayern have found a very capable backup. It's a good stylistic fit for the German giants, while for PSV, it's a club record departure.

Piero Hincapié

€40M (£34.5M; $46M)
Bayer Leverkusen: C

Arsenal: A

Hincapié's loan to Arsenal has become a permanent move after certain conditions were met. He proved an excellent pickup last summer, ably sharing the left-back role with Riccardo Calafiori and covering at center back too.

Factoring in the initial loan fee of €6 million, this looks to have cost the Gunners just shy of €50 million all in. For a player of this established quality and age (24), it goes down as an absolute bargain.

Emmanuel Emegha

€25M (£22M; $29M)
Strasbourg: B

Chelsea: B

Chelsea struck a deal to sign Emegha in the summer of 2025, but opted to let him stay at sister club Strasbourg and continue developing for another year. It was a good idea, but things didn't go to plan as the Dutchman missed most of last season due to injury.

For a player who stands at 6-foot-5, he is extremely fast, with great movement, but he is unreliable in front of goal and underperformed his xG by three in 2024-25. Emegha has huge potential and is still only 23, but he probably isn't ready to start for Chelsea just yet.

Robert Lewandowski

Free transfer
Barcelona: B

Chicago Fire FC: B+

The Chicago Fire won the race to sign legendary striker Lewandowski, who may be into his late 30s but still scored 14 goals from 17 starts in LaLiga last season. He'll join MLS top scorer Hugo Cuypers (13 goals this term) in what is now a fearsome front two on paper.

It was certainly time for him to depart Barcelona, where he excelled since joining in 2022, but also accounted for a huge portion of the wage bill at a club that's been right up against it financially for some time.

Bernardo Silva

Free
Manchester City: D

Real Madrid: A

Silva, who is one of the most tactically versatile and intelligent players the sport has ever seen, was linked strongly to each of Spain's big three clubs. But Los Blancos will benefit hugely from his presence in a variety of ways.

After nine incredible years at City, there was little need for the club to recoup any sort of fee for him, but this one still really hurts. The Portugal midfielder was a crucial component of the team and the dressing room and a symbol of the Pep Guardiola era.

Ibrahima Konaté

Free
Liverpool: D

Real Madrid: B-

Konaté's athleticism is off the charts, and when he's in good form, he's close to unbeatable at the back. But inconsistency has long troubled his game, and reports in Spain suggest not only has he earned a huge signing bonus of €20 million, but he's more than tripled his weekly wage with this move.

From Madrid's perspective, this is no free transfer. But from Liverpool's perspective it is. They get absolutely nothing in return for a very good player, but have at least covered themselves for this eventuality with new €70 million arrival Jérémy Jacquet (agreed in January).

Antoine Griezmann

Free
Atletico Madrid: B

Orlando City: A

Griezmann's long farewell to Atlético was a tearjerker, and it feels right that the 35-year-old forward opted for a new challenge, on a different continent, rather than moved to another European club. He was a great servant to the club for a long time, negating the need to receive any kind of fee for him.

Orlando have had a poor campaign to date and could use all the help they can get; Griezmann's quality and personality is a great start to turning things around.

June 30

Gonçalo Ramos

€74M ($84M)
PSG: A

AC Milan: C+

First, Milan appointed former Manchester United manager Rúben Amorim as coach. Then they handed him his first new weapon: Ramos, a Champions League winner and a potent goal scorer -- albeit via a bit-part role with PSG these past three years.

This is a gargantuan outlay from the Italian giants, who have smashed their transfer record by more than €20 million for a player who has too often found himself kicking his heels for club and country of late. PSG, meanwhile, have banked €74 million, potentially rising to around €80 million, for a squad player; they'll rightly be delighted with that.

Alejandro Grimaldo

€20M ($22.7M)
Bayer Leverkusen: C

Atlético Madrid: A

Grimaldo will finally play in Spain's top tier, having left Barcelona's academy in 2016 without a first-team appearance to his name. He's blossomed abroad, at both Benfica and Bayer Leverkusen, developing into one of the best attacking fullbacks in the game. At €20 million, this is a steal for Atleti -- even if he is 30 years old.

Leverkusen don't stand a chance of replacing his quality like-for-like with a humble fee, and they've reluctantly said goodbye to one of their best players during that famous unbeaten title run in 2023-24.

June 18

Jan Paul van Hecke

£52M ($70M)
Brighton & Hove Albion: B+

Tottenham: B

Van Hecke has slowly developed into one of the Premier League's best center backs. The Netherlands international has long been one of the best passers and dribblers from the back, and now he's become a sturdier, meaner defender, too.

At 25, he's ready for the next step, and reuniting with manager Roberto De Zerbi at Tottenham feels like a brilliant match. Brighton were resigned to losing him given he had just one year left on his contract and did well to hold out for a fee above £50 million.

Víctor Muñoz

€40M (£35M; $46M)
Osasuna: B+

Liverpool: B-

Muñoz is an incredibly busy, buzzing winger who tears around the pitch, tries to beat defenders one-on-one and shoots willingly. Stylistically that makes him a good fit for Andoni Iraola, but Liverpool are gambling slightly on the 23-year-old stepping up to the elite level quickly.

For Osasuna, this is a record departure -- but not quite the huge payday it looks like. They only hold 50% of the player's rights, with Real Madrid holding the other half; that means half €40M fee will go to Los Blancos.

June 15

Marcos Senesi

Free
Bournemouth: D

Tottenham: A

Senesi was one of the outstanding center backs in the Premier League last season. A committed defender, a physical presence and a brilliant passer from the back, he stood out as one of the best free agents heading into the summer, and Spurs have won the race for his signature.

His signing does raise some questions for the club to answer. Will captain Cristian Romero be departing? Is the plan to play with two left-footers (Senesi and Micky van de Ven), or will it be a back three? Though none of that detracts from the fact this deal is a coup.

Andy Robertson

Free
Liverpool: B

Tottenham: B

Tottenham came close to signing Robertson in January and have now finally sealed the deal. The 32-year-old defender's time at Liverpool had come to a natural end as he passed his peak and Milos Kerkez replaced him in the XI.

Roberto De Zerbi will value the Scotland international's passing ability and the Spurs squad badly need his leadership qualities -- although they have reportedly paid a premium in wages for a player who won't necessarily be first choice.

June 29

Rasmus Højlund

€44M (£38M; $51M)
Manchester United: B+

Napoli: B+

Højlund's loan to Napoli was made permanent the moment the Italian giants qualified for the Champions League. The Denmark striker led the attacking line all season long, contributing 16 goals in total, and rebounded well from his disappointing spell at Man United.

It's a good deal for both clubs, as €44 million (plus a €6 million loan fee last season) for a reliable goal scorer represents strong value for Napoli, while United will be pleased to make a fair chunk of their money back on a signing that cost them an initial €75 million and simply did not work out.

stories.headline: What Los Angeles Angels sale means for franchise, MLB
stories.summary: After 23 years, Arte Moreno has agreed to sell the Angels. What will new owner Stan Kroenke bring to baseball in Anaheim?
stories.body:
After 23 years, Arte Moreno is selling the Los Angeles Angels.

Stan Kroenke -- whose company, Kroenke Sports & Entertainment, owns the NFL's Los Angeles Rams, the NBA's Denver Nuggets and the NHL's Colorado Avalanche -- agreed Tuesday to acquire a controlling interest in the team from Moreno.

Under Moreno, MLB's first Latino majority owner, the Angels made the postseason six times, but haven't played meaningful October baseball since 2014 -- despite the presence of Mike Trout, one of the greatest players of his generation. The team also let two-way superstar Shohei Ohtani walk after the 2023 season, when he signed with the rival Los Angeles Dodgers.

What does this deal mean for the Angels? For Major League Baseball? ESPN MLB experts Alden Gonzalez and Buster Olney break it down.

Who is Stan Kroenke?

Gonzalez: A man who clearly aspires to run sports in Southern California. Kroenke, 79, presides over the NFL's L.A. Rams and has now taken control of the Angels in neighboring Orange County. According to Forbes, he is worth approximately $24.3 billion. (Moreno, for reference, is worth $5 billion. New York Mets owner Steve Cohen, meanwhile, is worth $23 billion.) Kroenke is a real estate magnate who married a Walmart heiress and, all told, owns eight sports franchises. Four of them (the Nuggets, Avalanche, Rapids of MLS and Mammoth of the National Lacrosse League) are based in Colorado. The other two are in England: Arsenal F.C. of the Premier League and Arsenal W.F.C. of the Women's Super League.

What is Kroenke's track record as an owner of teams in other major sports?

Gonzalez: Kroenke's teams have won two Super Bowls, two Stanley Cups, an NBA title, an MLS Cup, two NLL championships and, most recently, a Premier League championship.

If you talk to L.A. Rams fans, he is a godsend. If you talk to fans of the NFL franchise when it was based in St. Louis, he is public enemy No. 1. If you ask Arsenal fans, he is an absentee owner. If he is heavily involved in the Angels, though, it would probably be a good thing. How involved he actually will be remains to be seen.

What could this mean for the future of the Angels?

Gonzalez: If the Rams offer up any evidence, Angels fans should be really excited. When Kroenke helped move the Rams from St. Louis back to L.A., he recognized that he needed to not just win but do so with stars. He traded up to the first overall pick to land Jared Goff, hired the NFL's youngest coach in Sean McVay, and later encouraged his general manager, Les Snead, to bring in top-tier talent, no matter the cost.

In other words, Kroenke thought boldly, never more so than by engineering the construction of SoFi Stadium at the heart of a 300-acre sports-and-entertainment hub. The Angels need that type of boldness. For too long, they'd grown stale.

Olney: The Angels are going to be in a better place, undoubtedly, because Moreno had become one of the least effective owners in Major League Baseball, with his unusual management style. He would occasionally drop in and hijack negotiations to land expensive sluggers -- Josh Hamilton and Albert Pujols, for example -- who would greatly complicate the team's payroll situation, and he'd cut operating expenses in other parts of the organization, leaving the general managers to clean up the mess.

In another famous example of his meddling, he refused to allow former GM Perry Minasian to trade Shohei Ohtani when it was apparent that Ohtani was headed to free agency.

Does this make it more likely Mike Trout will be playing playoff baseball in the near future?

Gonzalez: First of all, does Mike Trout want to stay with the Angels? Without having heard from Trout himself, my gut reaction is yes. It has been obvious for a while that Trout does not want to leave the Angels or, just as relevant, his summer spot in Orange County. What would drive him out would be a lack of hope that the Angels as an organization could turn this around.

But he has hope now. John Mozeliak came in as a consultant and began to do things differently, and now Kroenke comes in with the reputation of building the Rams into a powerhouse just 35 miles north. It was already going to be exceedingly difficult to find a taker for Trout's contract, which will pay him $141.8 million from 2027 to 2030. Perhaps now, at least for another year, that won't be necessary.

Olney: One way or another, absolutely. Trout always has the option to try to force his way off the Angels, and a new owner is more likely to consider that path than Moreno, who was never going to trade a future inner-circle Hall of Famer and the face of his franchise -- and so that could now be a more viable option. If Trout stays -- and that seems more likely -- then the Angels are bound to be more effectively run going into the future. Let's put it more bluntly: It's impossible for Kroenke to run baseball operations worse than Morena has during Trout's career.

What is Arte Moreno's legacy as an owner?

Gonzalez: Moreno's legacy can essentially be split into two chapters. The first was rosy. He came in off the heels of a championship in 2003 and quickly won the adoration of the fans, signing Vladimir Guerrero and Bartolo Colon, lowering beer prices and presiding over the most successful run in franchise history, one that included five division titles in a six-year stretch from 2004 to 2009. By the end of 2011, Moreno had built the Angels into the type of franchise worthy of commanding a 20-year, $3 billion television deal.

Then things got stale. Their big free agents flopped, their player development pipeline stalled, and Moreno started to get panned for wielding too much control over baseball operations and being stingy in every aspect of the organization outside of the payroll. Throughout 2026, as the Angels floundered through another miserable season, "sell the team" chants were a constant at Angel Stadium. Moreno became arguably the most hated owner in MLB.

Olney: A missed opportunity. Trout and Ohtani are two all-time great baseball talents, playing in a market that could easily sustain a big-market payroll, and the Angels didn't win a single postseason game with one or both of them. There was a time early in Moreno's tenure when the Angels were regarded as a good, progressive organization, and Moreno let them fall far behind the times -- and now they have a long way to go to catch up to the standard the Dodgers have established in Southern California.

Does another MLB team being sold have any bearing on baseball's labor negotiations?

Gonzalez: It won't change MLB's push for a salary cap, but it will turn up the volume on the players' retort. To players, the Padres selling for a record $3.9 billion proved what many of them firmly believe -- that if you invest in the product, like late Padres owner Peter Seidler did, fans will come, revenues will follow, and worst case, you can sell the team for far more than you bought it for.

The Angels topped that valuation, a source with knowledge of the situation said, even though they have long fielded a miserable on-field product. To players, it only bolsters their case that baseball is a good business, and that a salary cap is not needed to boost franchise values.

Olney: I think the sale prices for the Padres and Angels will embolden the owners even more in their quest for a salary cap, in the belief that a massive overhaul of the sport's economic system -- in which cost certainty becomes the priority -- will enhance franchise values even more. It's possible that Moreno, who has been a front-line warrior in past labor negotiations, was less interested in wading through a fight, but other owners will see that effort as a way to even more wealth.

stories.headline: 2026 WNBA championship odds: Lynx still odds-on title favorites; Aces, Valkyries next
stories.summary: The Lynx remain odds-on favorites to win the WNBA championship, while the red-hot Valkyries are back up to third on the oddsboard.
stories.body:
The Minnesota Lynx are still the odds-on favorites to win the 2026 WNBA Finals headed into the FIBA World Cup break, showing -110 odds, slightly longer than the -115 they had a week prior. That could have something to do with the resurgent Golden State Valkyries notching four wins in a row going into the break -- including a big one over Minnesota -- to improve them to a third-best +700.

The Las Vegas Aces have maintained second place at +600 on the championship odds board, while the Atlanta Dream and Indiana Fever are tied for fifth at +850. The New York Liberty continue to drift, now out to 15-1, after opening the season as the +220 favorite.

The Dallas Wings and Washington Mystics round out the board at 70-1. There are no teams beyond that with the playoff teams being officially set heading into the final month of the regular season.

Odds by DraftKings and subject to change.

Regular-season MVP
A'ja Wilson -1200

Olivia Miles +800

Kelsey Mitchell 40-1

Caitlin Clark 50-1

Paige Bueckers 200-1

Breanna Stewart 250-1

stories.headline: 'The Hoop Collective': Episodes of Brian Windhorst's NBA podcast
stories.summary: Here are the top highlights from Brian Windhorst's "The Hoop Collective" podcast, from breaking news to the latest intel and reaction from around the NBA.
stories.body:
"The Hoop Collective" podcast, hosted by ESPN's Brian Windhorst, releases episodes every Monday, Wednesday and Friday during the NBA season and Tuesday and Friday during the offseason. Windhorst and his guests break down what's happening on and off the court, evaluating the trends you need to know and examining the latest news from across the NBA.

Listen to 'The Hoop Collective':

ESPN | Spotify | YouTube | Apple | Amazon | iHeartMedia | TuneIn

Latest episodes:

Sept. 1 |Aug. 28 | Aug. 25 | Aug. 21 | Aug. 18

Quick links:

Schedule | Standings | Stats | Transactions

'The Hoop Collective' episodes

Sept. 1: How Steph Curry can decide Warriors' future and major questions for Pistons
Brian is joined by ESPN's Tim MacMahon and Anthony Slater to discuss Stephen Curry's future with the Golden State Warriors, including how a potential extension could determine the franchise's outlook. They then move on to the Jalen Duren-Detroit Pistons situation, as his restricted free agency continues. Will this cause major issues for the Pistons' season? They close on the recent dramatic FIBA World Cup qualifiers, including a matchup between Victor Wembanyama and Nikola Jokic.

Topics:

2:09: Latest on Steph Curry's future in Golden State

8:31: How Steph could help the Warriors' chances

20:16: Jalen Duren and Pistons still stuck in negotiations

26:13: What is the worst-case scenario for Detroit?

40:40: Windy Storytime: Cavs contract standoff

46:06: Headlines from FIBA World Cup qualifiers

46:48: Epic battle between Wembanyama and Jokic

49:39: Other NBA stars making an impact in FIBA

Slater on the potential Curry extension in Golden State and why he could wait: "One of the things in discussions I've been having with people is this idea of, let's say he's like, '[Taking less money for the team is] something I'd think about.' I would be surprised if he locked into a number now because, as you just saw with Draymond Green, the Warriors and their legendary figures are willing to trust each other in business.

"Draymond Green willingly gave up $27 million and went into unrestricted free agency where he couldn't have got $27 million back, [but] under the understanding if business didn't work out, he would get that money back. If you're Steph, you say, 'OK, you know what? I'll give y'all a crack at going and trying to find some stuff, but if you don't, at the end of the day, if I come back and say, give me the full max, I get the full max.'

"So, to answer your question, he doesn't have to necessarily lock into it now because they can't really execute [upgrading the roster]. stories.headline: Song Yadong KO's Umar Nurmagomedov in massive UFC upset
stories.summary: Song Yadong pulled off a massive upset by knocking out heavily favored Umar Nurmagomedov in the men's bantamweight main event of UFC Fight Night in Shanghai.
stories.body:
Song Yadong saved the greatest performance of his career for his home country, knocking out former title challenger Umar Nurmagomedov in the men's bantamweight main event of UFC Fight Night on Saturday in Shanghai.

Song (24-9-1, 1 NC), a nearly 5-1 underdog at DraftKings Sportsbook, dropped Nurmagomedov with a short right hand, drawing a roar from the crowd when the fight was waved off at 1 minute, 48 seconds of Round 2.

"I believe in myself, and my team believed that I would win this fight," Song said through an interpreter. "They told me I would knock this guy out, and I did it."

It was the second straight fight in China for Song and his second straight win by finish. His most recent knockout win had been in 2023.

Song, making his first appearance in Shanghai since his UFC debut at age 19 in 2017, walked out to a hero's welcome.

"Nine years ago, I wanted to show I could walk in this Octagon," he said. "Nine years later, I want to prove I am the best in the world. I am the best Chinese fighter in the world."

The knockout came after Nurmagomedov (20-2) ducked out of the way of a left hand and right into the path of a short right hand, which connected near his right ear and sent him limply to the canvas. Song delivered three finishing shots on the mat before the referee jumped in.

That sent Song running around inside the cage in celebration, where he nearly ran into Nurmagomedov's younger brother and cornerman, PFL lightweight champion Usman Nurmagomedov, who had rushed in to check on his fallen brother. Usman Nurmagomedov appeared to throw an elbow in Song's direction as the elated winner was running past.

Song climbed atop the cage to soak in the fans' cheers before jumping down outside the cage and running into the crowd to get hugs and high-fives from fans.

"Maybe not today, maybe not tomorrow, maybe not next month, but I will be the first male Chinese UFC champion," Song said through the interpreter, with the "male" designation a nod to countrywoman Zhang Weili, a two-time women's champion at strawweight.

Song, who trains in Sacramento, California, switched to English and yelled, "Give me the title shot!"

stories.headline: Sources: Southampton loans USMNT's Downs to St. Louis
stories.summary: St. Louis City SC is set to acquire United States forward Damion Downs on loan from English Championship side Southampton, a source with direct knowledge of the deal confirmed to ESPN.
stories.body:
St. Louis City SC is set to acquire United States forward Damion Downs on loan from English Championship side Southampton, a source with direct knowledge of the deal confirmed to ESPN.

Downs, 22, is looking for a fresh start after failing to find the net for the Saints since the club acquired him in July of 2025. He has yet to appear for the club in the Championship so far this season.

The U.S. international appeared to be on the rise after scoring 11 goals in all competitions for FC Cologne during the 2024-25 season. A spot with the USMNT for the 2025 Gold Cup followed, and he scored the winning penalty in the shootout victory over Costa Rica in the quarterfinals.

But Downs' last goal at club level came during the aforementioned campaign with Cologne. Not even a return to the Bundesliga last season on loan with Hamburg SV, which saw him make 12 appearances, was enough to revive his fortunes.

Downs will find the competition for places intense given the team's likely capture of Colorado Rapids forward Rafael Navarro. St. Louis has also been among the hotter teams in MLS, having gone unbeaten in its last 12 league matches, and moving up to sixth place in the Western Conference.

Downs has made a total of six appearances for the USMNT. He was born in Germany to an American father and German mother and spent some of his childhood in the United States.

The Athletic was the first to report the news of Downs' loan to St. Louis.

stories.headline: What makes Max Verstappen so good? Career, background and F1 records
stories.summary: Max Verstappen is returning to his racing roots and is facing 100 drivers in a unique event called Max vs. 100 where the Formula 1 star will attempt to overtake 100 challengers, starting from the back of the grid.
stories.body:
Max Verstappen is returning to his racing roots and is taking part in a unique event called Max vs 100 where the Formula 1 star will attempt to overtake 100 drivers, starting from the back of the grid.

The 28-year-old currently races in F1, the highest tier in motorsport. He is one of the fiercest competitors out there and is known for his aggressive driving style and fearless overtaking.

But if you have never heard of him, or want to learn more, here is everything you need to know.

- Max vs 100: F1 superstar Verstappen to race drivers in karting event - live on Disney+

Who is Max Verstappen?
Verstappen was born in Belgium to his Dutch father Jos and his Belgian mother Sophie. His father raced in F1 between 1994-2003 and had two podium finishes, while his mother competed in karts. He currently resides in Monaco.

Who does he race for?
Verstappen started racing go-karts when he was just four years old and started to compete in championships at seven.

He then made his way through the ranks winning several world and European titles in 2013. He raced just one season in Formula 3 before skipping Formula 2 and heading straight to Formula 1.

In 2015, he signed for Red Bull junior team Toro Rosso at the age of 17 before he was promoted to Red Bull a year later.

He then went on to become the youngest ever grand prix winner after taking victory at the Spanish Grand Prix and has been at Red Bull ever since, becoming the most successful driver at the team.

He signed a long-term contract back in March 2022 to stay at the Milton Keynes-based team until the end of 2028, and before the Dutch Grand Prix this year he penned a new deal keeping him at the team until 2030.

What has he achieved?
It was clear from the early days that Verstappen was going to be an exceptional racing driver and he's become a phenomenon since with a killer instinct.

He's had 244 race starts in F1 and has been on the top step of the podium 71 times. He's been on the podium 131 times and is just two pole positions away from reaching 50 career poles.

The Dutchman has four world championships which he won back-to-back in a dominant Red Bull era between 2021-2024.

He also has an impressive list of achievements to his name, one being in 2023 where he recorded the most wins [19] and the most podium finishes [21] in a single season. He also recorded 10 consecutive race victories.

When is Max vs 100?
The event is taking place on Sept. 16 and will be streamed live on Disney+.

Why is he racing in Max vs 100?

Verstappen has never been shy of getting his teeth stuck into other forms of motorsport away from Formula 1. He most recently made his debut at the iconic Nürburgring 24 Hours in May, driving a Mercedes-AMG GT3.

This will be a slightly different challenge for the Dutchman, but no doubt one he will enjoy with his competitive nature.

"In go-karts you learn all the basics: starts, defending, overtaking," Verstappen said. "Of course, I spent a long period of my life go-karting, so it's always nice to return."

The event is taking place at Silverstone in the U.K. and a circuit has been purpose-built for the occasion. It's set to be the biggest go-kart event in the world.

- Max Verstappen deal: Good news for Red Bull and F1, bad news for the driver market

- Max Verstappen ends F1 speculation by signing new Red Bull contract to 2030

How is his 2026 F1 season going?
The 2026 season is one with big regulation and rules changes and Red Bull are currently at the back of the front running teams, but are ahead of the midfield pack.

Verstappen is still searching for his first race win of the season, but has been on the podium four times.

He's currently sixth in the title championship and is 130 points adrift from title leader Kimi Antonelli.

stories.headline: AFL overreactions: Will Pendlebury's legacy be tarnished with a move to the Suns?
stories.summary: The big news this week was that Scott Pendlebury would depart Collingwood and join Gold Coast on a playing-then-coaching deal. But will this move tarnish his legacy as a Collingwood and AFL legend? Let's get to this week's big talking point.
stories.body:
There are plenty of talking points after the AFL's wildcard weekend, with one of the biggest being the announcement Scott Pendlebury would depart Collingwood and join Gold Coast likely on a playing-then-coaching deal.

Let's get to this week's overreactions column, where we judge the biggest takeaways as legitimate or irrational.

Scott Pendlebury's legacy will be tarnished by not being a one-club player
The football world was left stunned on Sunday morning when news broke that Collingwood champion Scott Pendlebury would be departing the club and continuing his playing career at Gold Coast.

It's understood the 442-game veteran was eager to remain at the Magpies but a contract extension reportedly never arrived, leading Pendlebury to explore other playing opportunities for 2027. With his move to the Suns now all but confirmed, he is no longer set to be the one-club player many believed he would retire as, and that's led to questions and concerns about his legacy.

Verdict: Overreaction

So what if Pendlebury isn't a one-club player. Sam Mitchell isn't a one-club player and nobody would associate him with any club other than Hawthorn. Luke Hodge's name carries the same weight around Hawthron even though he finished his career at the Lioins. It's also easy to forget that Nathan Buckley once upon a time played for Brisbane.

Pendlebury has built up enough credits over his 20-year career where his legendary footballing legacy is secure. There's pretty much nothing he can do that would taint his image as one of the most revered and respected players in league history.

It's 2026, and the long-held concept of player loyalty isn't the same as it once was. With football being the business it is, loyalty can often be a one-way street. It's always a savvy and responsible move for players to look after their futures.

Extending his career at another club certainly shouldn't be viewed as a negative. In fact, who's to say taking this path won't ultimately enhance his legacy?

What would a premiership at the Suns mean for Pendlebury? It has to add to his story in a positive way. I'm not saying that's happening next season but it proves his legacy is still being written.

-- Jake Michaels

stories.headline: Jets star goalie Connor Hellebuyck confirms trade request
stories.summary: Three-time Vezina Trophy-winning goaltender Connor Hellebuyck publicly confirmed Thursday that he asked the Winnipeg Jets to trade him.
stories.body:
WINNIPEG, Manitoba -- Three-time Vezina Trophy-winning goaltender Connor Hellebuyck publicly confirmed Thursday that he asked the Winnipeg Jets to trade him.

In a statement released by his agent, Ray Petkau, Hellebuyck said he made the request several months ago and "tried to handle the situation quietly and respectfully while giving the organization time to explore its options."

Hellebuyck said he felt it was important to go public because training camp is fast approaching. Camps are set to open in roughly three weeks.

"My position has not changed, and I believe moving on is the best path forward for me and my family," Hellebuyck said. "(I) hope a resolution can be reached soon."

Hellebuyck, 33, has played his entire NHL career with the Jets and was voted MVP in the 2024-25 season. He backstopped the U.S. to the gold medal at the Olympics in February.

A team spokesperson did not immediately respond to a message seeking comment.

Trade rumors swirled about Hellebuyck in late June around the draft, but nothing came to fruition. The Michigan native missed time because of injury and had a career-worst .895 save percentage last season as Winnipeg underachieved expectations and missed the playoffs.

But his track record and body of work are among the best at the position over the past decade. His 345 wins, 2.58 goals-against average and .916 save percentage since entering the league in 2015 are second only to Tampa Bay two-time Stanley Cup champion Andrei Vasilevskiy.

Hellebuyck has not enjoyed the same postseason success as Vasilevskiy and the Lightning. He's 24-34, with the Jets only making it past the second round and into the Western Conference final once, back in 2018.

He signed an eight-year, $59.5 million extension with Winnipeg in October 2023. He's under contract through 2031 at a salary cap hit of $8.5 million.

"Winnipeg has been my home for my entire NHL career, and I will always be grateful for my time there," Hellebuyck said. "I appreciate everything Winnipeg Jets fans have meant to me throughout my career."

stories.headline: Roosters rest nine players including new halves duo
stories.summary: The Sydney Roosters' new halves combination will go into the finals cold after the Tricolours rested Hugo Savala, Daly Cherry-Evans and seven other players from the last round of the NRL regular season.
stories.body:
The Sydney Roosters' new halves combination will go into the finals cold after the Tricolours rested Hugo Savala, Daly Cherry-Evans and seven other players from the last round of the NRL regular season.

With a top-four finish already secured, the Roosters have named second-gamers Toby Rodwell and Reece Foley as their starting halves to face South Sydney on Friday night.

Billy Smith, James Tedesco, Mark Nawaqanitawase, Naufahu Whyte, Reece Robson, Rob Toia and Siua Wong all drop out as the Roosters eye as healthy a team as possible for the finals.

But the upshot is that Savala and Cherry-Evans will not have a dress rehearsal before the play-offs, when they will be tasked with steering the ship in the absence of injured halfback Sam Walker.

Savala and Cherry-Evans have started in the halves together only twice before, most recently in the round-19 defeat of Parramatta, and will reunite against either the Warriors or Penrith for a week-one qualifying final.

Roosters veteran Daniel Tupou has recovered from a shoulder injury for his first game since July, but Angus Crichton (foot) and Victor Radley (concussion) remain out for round 27.

Souths have recalled fullback Jye Gray to the starting line-up and promoted Latrell Mitchell back to centre after he returned from injury via the bench last week.

Tallis Duncan is rested amid a breakout season.

The third-placed Dolphins have lost star winger Selwyn Cobbo to an ankle injury for their last game of the regular season, bringing Tevita Naufahu into the starting side against Gold Coast.

Despite locking up a top-two finish, Penrith have resisted the urge to rest players en masse, naming their best available team in pursuit of the minor premiership.

The Panthers also have three-time premiership winner Mitch Kenny back from a leg injury for his first game since April, and have included Isaah Yeo in their extended squad.

Yeo is considered unlikely to return from his pectoral injury against Wests Tigers this Sunday, however.

The Panthers have also named the late John Farragher in jersey 23 on their team sheet, after the long-time clubman and former player died last year, aged 68.

Paul Alamoti remains sidelined with a hamstring issue, while Luke Garner replaces Izack Tago (knee) at starting centre.

Penrith's minor premiership rivals the Warriors have Chanel Harris-Tavita and Te Maire Martin back from hamstring problems to start in the halves against Manly.

But Kurt Capewell and Wayde Egan have been rested at the end of taxing seasons, while Jett Cleary drops to the extended bench after an impressive NRL debut.

Cronulla have named centre Michael Gabrael and five-eighth Riley Pollard for NRL debuts as Nicho Hynes, Blayke Brailey and Teig Wilton all rest before the finals.

Club debutant Riley Jones also comes into the centres to face Melbourne after Mawene Hiroti suffered a rib injury against Parramatta last week.

Robert Derby replaces Zac Laybutt (head knock) on the wing as eighth-placed North Queensland host Canberra.
